Is DEMO-34 still In progress because more work is planned on it, or did the card simply not move when the pull request was ready?

Why:
- DEMO-34: acme/shop#202 has been open and ready for 5 days with no review and no activity. The build passes, so the build is not holding reviewers back. (GitHub)
- DEMO-34: Tom's comment 5 days ago says it is 'bigger than planned', touching the basket, checkout and order emails. The card has stayed in In progress since 14 days ago, so it is not in the Review column. (Jira)
- DEMO-34: The pull request is 920 lines across 23 files. The finished item DEMO-76, at 796 lines and 20 files, also had the slowest first look of any finished item (2.4 days). (Board)
- Ruled out: DEMO-89, DEMO-90: Not a general queue: the other two open pull requests got a first look after 17 hours (acme/shop#206) and 1 day (acme/shop#207). (GitHub)
- Ruled out: DEMO-35: DEMO-35 is not waiting for review. It is a draft, and Priya's comment 3 days ago says it is blocked by ACC-118, which is still In progress. (Jira)

Options:
A. Agree that the card moves to Review when the pull request is ready, and that a first look comes within one working day. Name a reviewer for any pull request still unseen at the next daily check. Needs a daily glance at the Review column and a little interruption of current work. Check: Every pull request ready from now on gets a first review within one working day, checked at the next refresh. (recommended)
B. Ask Tom to split DEMO-34 into smaller pull requests by area: basket, checkout, order emails. Some rework and a merge order to plan, but each part is far easier to review. Check: The first smaller pull request for DEMO-34 gets a review within one working day of being ready. (recommended)
C. Have a reviewer start on acme/shop#202 now as it is, ahead of new work. Reviewing 23 files takes a long block of someone's time, and it won't change how the next big change is handled. Check: acme/shop#202 has its first review by the next refresh.
Recommended because A fixes the visibility gap that left DEMO-34 unseen, and B removes the size that makes it hard to pick up.

answers.question:
2 items are merged but not Done
Their code was merged 2 to 4 days ago, but the cards are still in progress. Either testing happens after the merge, or the cards were not moved.

Items are merged but still in progress on the board. Check for each whether testing happens after the merge or the card was not moved, and propose the smallest board or policy change. Cite relevant ticket evidence, distinguish observed facts from possible causes, and end with a concrete team action and a measurable checkpoint.
answers.message:
DEMO-31 and DEMO-30 look like **cards moved late, not testing after the merge**: both entered In progress only after their pull requests were ready.
Likely · Jira + GitHub: Jira and GitHub agree.

Does the team test anything after a merge, and if so where does that show on the board?

Why:
- DEMO-31: The card went from Backlog to In progress 5 days ago and never visited Review. The pull request was ready 8 days ago, so work started before the card moved. (Jira)
- DEMO-30: The card moved to In progress 2 days ago, the same time its pull request merged (2 days ago). The pull request was ready 7 days ago. (Jira)
- DEMO-31, DEMO-30: acme/shop#204 merged 4 days ago and acme/shop#205 merged 2 days ago. Both were approved without requested changes, so no code rework explains the wait. (GitHub)
- Ruled out: DEMO-31, DEMO-30: Nothing shows testing after the merge. Neither card has comments, links or a testing status in its history. Only the assignees can confirm that no manual check happens. (Jira)

Options:
A. Ask Tom and Ana whether anything remains after the merge, then move both cards to Done. Costs one short conversation each. Fixes only these two cards. Check: DEMO-31 and DEMO-30 are out of In progress by the next refresh. (recommended)
B. Agree that a card moves to Review when its pull request is ready and to Done when it merges. Add a Jira-GitHub automation rule if one is available. Needs a short team agreement. Automation needs someone to set it up. Check: For the next five merged items, the card leaves In progress within a day of the merge. (recommended)
C. Add a Testing column only if Tom or Ana say a check really happens after the merge. Adds a column and a handoff. Do it only if the answer is yes. Check: Merged cards show a Testing visit, and DEMO-31 and DEMO-30 do too.
Recommended because A clears these two cards today, and B stops the board lagging the code on the next ones.

answers.label: What is the failing build holding up?
answers.question:
An approved pull request is held by failing checks
DEMO-33: the checks on its latest commit fail. It is already approved, so only the checks stand between it and the merge.

Pull requests have failing checks on their latest commit. For each, say how long it has been open, whether it is already approved, and what the red build holds back on the board. Propose the smallest team agreement, such as fixing a red build before new work, with a measurable checkpoint. Never blame whoever wrote the code. Cite relevant ticket evidence, distinguish observed facts from possible causes, and end with a concrete team action and a measurable checkpoint.
answers.message:
Only one pull request has a red build: **acme/shop#203 on DEMO-33**. It has been open 6 days and approved for 1, and the failing e2e test is the only thing holding the merge.
Likely · GitHub + Jira + Board: GitHub, Jira and the board agree.
Next step: Ask Ana and Jonas whether the failing e2e checkout test is flaky. If it is, rerun it or quarantine it today so acme/shop#203 can merge. Check: acme/shop#203 merged and DEMO-33 out of In progress by the next refresh. A green build on the latest commit.
Has the e2e checkout test failed on other pull requests recently, or only on acme/shop#203?

Why:
- DEMO-33: acme/shop#203 was ready for review 6 days ago, approved 1 day ago, with no changes requested. Checks on the latest commit fail. (GitHub)
- DEMO-33: Jonas commented 1 day ago: 'Approved. The e2e checkout test fails on CI but passes locally. Flaky?' This is a suspicion, not a confirmed cause. (Jira)
- DEMO-33: The card has sat in In progress for 11 days, past the usual 7. The board and the code disagree: the code is approved and only the build holds it. (Board)
- Ruled out: DEMO-33: Not a review delay or rework: first look came after 3 days, no changes were requested, and approval followed. Size is small at 140 lines in 4 files. (GitHub)
- Ruled out: DEMO-35, DEMO-90, DEMO-34, DEMO-89: No other pull request has a red build. acme/shop#201 and acme/shop#207 are still running checks. acme/shop#202 and acme/shop#206 pass. (GitHub)

Options:
A. Rerun the e2e checkout test on acme/shop#203 and merge if it goes green Cheap, but hides a real defect if the test is not flaky Check: acme/shop#203 merged and DEMO-33 moved on within 1 working day (recommended)
B. Agree that a red build on an approved pull request is looked at within one working day, before anyone starts new work Briefly slows new starts, since DEMO-30 and DEMO-31 are also waiting to move Check: No approved pull request with failing checks for more than 1 day at the next refresh (recommended)

Recommended because A clears the one blocked pull request now, and B is the smallest agreement that stops the next red build from sitting.
